Day 1
From Hotel: 15 min · 3 min → Gëlle Fra
1. Gëlle Fra
The Golden Lady — a gilded figure of victory atop a 21-metre granite obelisk on Place de la Constitution, raised in 1923 for Luxembourg's war volunteers and now the nation's symbol of freedom. Behind it opens the classic panorama over the Pétrusse valley and the Adolphe Bridge.
Read more
Open 24/7
~20 min
Place de la Constitution · Ville Haute
3 min · 2 min → Notre-Dame Cathedral
2. Notre-Dame Cathedral
Luxembourg's national cathedral, built by the Jesuits between 1613 and 1621 and crowned by three slender black spires. Inside are luminous stained glass, the venerated statue of the Comforter of the Afflicted, and a crypt holding the tombs of the Grand Ducal family.
Read more

~30 min

Rue Notre-Dame · Ville Haute
2 min · 4 min → Place Guillaume II
3. Place Guillaume II
The city's grand civic square, known to locals as the Knuedler, framed by the neoclassical Town Hall and centred on a bronze equestrian statue of Grand Duke William II. A produce market fills it on Wednesday and Saturday mornings — a relaxed first taste of the upper town.
Read more
Open 24/7
~30 min
Place Guillaume II · Ville Haute
3 min · 5 min → Grand Ducal Palace
4. Grand Ducal Palace
The official town residence of the Grand Duke, a richly ornamented Flemish-Renaissance facade from the 1570s and one of the city's most photographed buildings. A ceremonial sentry stands guard out front; the interior opens to guided tours only in high summer.
Read more
Open 24/7
~20 min
17 Rue du Marché-aux-Herbes · Ville Haute
10 min · 6 min → Pfaffenthal Panoramic Elevator
5. Pfaffenthal Panoramic Elevator
A free glass lift that drops 71 metres through the cliff face, linking the upper town near Pescatore park to the Pfaffenthal valley below. The ride and the open viewing platform deliver a thrilling head-on view of the viaduct, the ramparts and the Alzette gorge.
Read more

Day 2
From Hotel: 15 min · 5 min → Chemin de la Corniche
1. Chemin de la Corniche
A pedestrian promenade laid along the 17th-century ramparts, famously called "the most beautiful balcony in Europe." It hangs above the Alzette with sweeping views down into the Grund, across to Neumünster Abbey and the old Wenzel fortifications — the single best walk in the city.
Read more
Open 24/7
~30 min
Chemin de la Corniche · Ville Haute
2 min · 7 min → Bock Casemates
2. Bock Casemates
The honeycomb of underground galleries carved into the Bock promontory where Count Sigfried founded the city in 963. Austrian engineers turned it into kilometres of gun chambers and tunnels — the "Gibraltar of the North" — with loophole views over the valley. The fortress and old town are UNESCO World Heritage.
Read more

Montée de Clausen · Ville Haute
7 min · 5 min → Neumünster Abbey
3. Neumünster Abbey
A former Benedictine abbey of 1606 set on the Alzette in the lower town of Grund, now the Neimënster cultural centre. Wander the cloisters and riverside courtyards, look in on the free exhibitions, and take in the abbey against the cliffs and ramparts above — the prettiest corner of the city.
Read more

18 min · 13 min → Fort Thüngen
4. Fort Thüngen
The "Three Acorns" fort of 1733, its trio of round towers restored and standing guard at the edge of the Kirchberg plateau. The ramparts and tunnels are free to roam, and the Musée Dräi Eechelen inside traces the story of the great fortress from 1443 to its dismantling.

3 min · 2 min → Mudam
5. Mudam
Luxembourg's contemporary art museum, a luminous glass-and-stone pavilion that I. M. Pei built atop the old fort bastions. The rotating exhibitions are strong, but the building itself — all light wells and clean geometry rising from the ramparts — is the real draw.

Day 3
From Hotel: 16 min · 3 min → Adolphe Bridge
1. Adolphe Bridge
When it opened in 1903 its 84-metre stone arch was the longest in the world. The double-deck bridge carries the tram across the Pétrusse gorge and delivers the single most photographed view in the city — the span of honey-coloured stone framed by the valley below and the Ville Haute rising behind.
Read more
Open 24/7
~20 min
Pont Adolphe · Ville Haute
12 min · 9 min → Pétrusse Valley
2. Pétrusse Valley
The Pétrusse river carved a wooded gorge through the lower city, now a long public park threaded with footpaths under the ramparts. At its heart are the Pétrusse Casemates — 18th-century fortification galleries carved into the cliff, reachable from steps at Place de la Constitution.
Read more
Open 24/7
~45 min
Vallée de la Pétrusse · Ville Basse
19 min · 9 min → Villa Vauban
3. Villa Vauban
An 1873 Neoclassical villa in the city park that serves as Luxembourg's municipal art museum. Its permanent collection spans 17th-century Dutch and Flemish masters — van de Velde, Teniers, Nason — through 19th-century European painting in elegant period rooms.
Read more

18 Avenue Émile Reuter · Ville-Haute
14 min · 10 min → MNHA
4. MNHA
The national museum on the old Fish Market traces Luxembourg from pre-Roman times to the modern era. Standout pieces include a Gallo-Roman mosaic floor, Iron Age goldwork, medieval sculpture, and a collection of 19th-century Luxembourg landscape painting.

Local Tastes
Judd mat Gaardebounen
The national dish: smoked pork collar simmered and served with broad beans in a creamy sauce and potatoes. Hearty, rustic and on every traditional menu.
Um Dierfgen · Brasserie du Cercle
Gromperekichelcher
Crisp, spiced potato fritters shredded with onion and parsley, fried to order. A street-food staple of the city's markets and festivals — best eaten hot from the pan.
Glacis Market · Um Dierfgen
Quetschentaart
An autumn plum tart on a thin pastry base, a Luxembourg pâtisserie classic. Find it alongside the local cakes at the city's historic bakeries.
Oberweis · Namur

Getting Around

Foreign number: accepted.
Luxembourg's main app-based taxi service; useful for late-night journeys and reaching destinations not served by the free tram line.
webtaxi.lu
Tram
The single tram line runs from Cloche d'Or through the central station and Kirchberg, linking most of the sights — and it is free to ride.
Luxembourg has a tram system — operated by Luxtram. Line used on this trip: T1.

Day Trips by Train
Trier · Germany · 50 min
Germany's oldest city, founded by the Romans. The colossal Porta Nigra gate, the imperial baths, the basilica and the cathedral make a UNESCO-listed core that is an easy direct ride over the border.
book at: CFL or Omio
Metz · France · 50 min
An elegant French city of golden Jaumont stone, crowned by the soaring Cathédrale Saint-Étienne and its acres of stained glass, plus the bold Centre Pompidou-Metz. Fast trains run city-centre to city-centre.
book at: CFL or Omio
Vianden · 1 hr
A storybook village in the Our valley beneath one of Europe's finest hilltop castles, the restored Château de Vianden. Reached by train to Ettelbruck and a connecting bus through the Ardennes.
book at: CFL or Omio
Clervaux · 1 hr
A castle town deep in the northern Ardennes, home to the white château that houses Edward Steichen's "The Family of Man" photography exhibition, a UNESCO Memory of the World collection.
book at: CFL or Omio
Brussels · Belgium · 3h 10 min
Art Nouveau capital of Europe — Grand-Place, Manneken Pis, Musées Royaux des Beaux-Arts, and the Atomium. Direct intercity train via Liège with no changes required.
book at: cfl.lu or Omio

Heads Up
Grand Ducal Palace — Interior tours summer only
The interior opens to guided tours only from mid-July to the end of August; the rest of the year only the facade and the guard are visible.
Mudam — Closes Tuesday Not Monday
Unlike most city museums, which close Monday, Mudam closes on Tuesdays and stays open late on Wednesday until 9:00pm.
Bock Casemates — Timed 15-minute entry
Admission runs in 15-minute slots between 9:45am and 5:00pm, and the site closes on 25 December and 1 January.
Worth Knowing

A City on Two Levels

Luxembourg's secret is its verticality. Almost everything worth seeing sits on the same compact upper plateau, but the magic is in the gorges that fall away on every side — the Pétrusse and the Alzette carving green ravines straight through the middle of a national capital. Spend Day 1 looking down from the ramparts, then Day 2 walking the valleys you were looking at, and the city reassembles itself into three dimensions.

Lean on the fact that every bus, tram and train in the country is free to ride. There is no ticket to fumble and no fare to calculate — take the tram up to Kirchberg, ride the funicular and the glass lift between the upper town and the valley floor, and let the elevators do the climbing your legs would otherwise dread. It quietly turns a hilly city into an easy one.
